purpose.observed_action: uninterrupted failures then successful authentication from the same source

rules.description:
The same tenant+account had an uninterrupted run of failed sign-ins from one
source address (no success from that source in between), followed by a successful
sign-in from the same source. v2 (2026-11-20): v1 counted failures that were
interleaved with successes and spread across unrelated sources, which alerted on
ordinary intermittent failures (see docs/AUTH_RULE_EVALUATION.md). Speed is not
required: slow guessing still matches. Successful authentication is NOT evidence of
data access or exfiltration; the follow-up check reports whether data access was
observed within coverage.
rules.explanation: {group}: uninterrupted failures then a success from the same source within {window_s}s. No claim of data access is made.
false_positives: repeated typos from the user's own device (labeled benign scenario B2 still alerts)
missing_visibility_hints: attacks rotating source addresses for every attempt are not matched by this rule (known gap, see AUTH_RULE_EVALUATION.md)

reference.description: >=5 consecutive failures from one source for one tenant+account, then success from that source, within 24h

rules.required_evidence: Authentication records with tenant, account, outcome and source address
resolving_data: whether the source previously authenticated successfully for this account
resource access logs after the success
sources: Microsoft Security blog 2026-10-21: a successful authentication does not by itself show data access or exfiltration
rules.title: Uninterrupted failed sign-ins from one source, then success from that source

subprocesses with HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY pointing to the recording proxy
